title: Will and Witness
premise: Retired detective Zephyrine Kavanagh has built a quiet life around her failing bookshop, but the arrival of twin letters — one confessing to a thirty-year-old drowning, one promising a second death at an upcoming anniversary dinner — shatters her peace. The letters point to the wealthy Aldous family, whose patriarch's death was ruled accidental decades ago and whose matriarch is about to celebrate her seventieth birthday with all six surviving relatives under one roof. As Zephyrine reopens the old case, she discovers her late mentor was the original investigating officer who buried the truth, forcing her to choose between loyalty to his memory and justice for the drowned man. At the anniversary dinner, the promised second death nearly succeeds; Zephyrine exposes the killer as the family's devoted housekeeper, who has spent thirty years protecting the daughter who actually caused the drowning. In the end, Zephyrine chooses truth over every loyalty she holds, publishes what she knows, and finally lets go of her mentor's shadow.
about_author: Quentin Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. He lives in a coastal town much like the one in this novel, where he claims the fog writes better plots than he does.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Zephyrine Kavanagh, sorting through inventory in her failing bookshop, receives two letters in the same hand: one confessing to a murder disguised as a drowning in 1994, the other promising 'a second glass raised' at the Aldous anniversary dinner. Her POV establishes her restlessness beneath quiet routine. The emotional beat is the jolt of purpose returning to a woman who thought her detecting days were over.

chapters.title: The Drowned Year
chapters.summary: Zephyrine digs into the 1994 case file of Thomas Ellery, a groundskeeper found dead in the Aldous estate's lake, ruled accidental by police — and signed off by her late mentor, Inspector Callum Reeve. Third-person limited follows her through archives and old newspaper clippings. The beat is dawning dread: the man who taught her everything may have buried a murder.

chapters.title: Six Under One Roof
chapters.summary: Posing as a rare-book appraiser invited to value the Aldous library, Zephyrine meets the family: matriarch Vivienne, brittle son Marcus, sharp-tongued daughter Cordelia, and three others circling old resentments. Her POV catalogs alibis and tells. The emotional beat is the seduction and sickness of wealth — belonging offered on terms that require blindness.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Silence
chapters.summary: Zephyrine notices Agnes Pryce, the family housekeeper of forty years, watching everyone and speaking to no one. A second-person-tinged chapter follows Zephyrine's instinct that servants see what families hide. She finds Thomas Ellery's name scratched inside a servant's corridor book. The beat is quiet menace: the house itself seems to be keeping secrets.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: Interviewing each sibling separately, Zephyrine discovers their 1994 alibis are identical down to phrasing — rehearsed. Marcus threatens her; Cordelia flirts with confession then retreats. Her POV tightens with frustration as the wall of coordinated silence holds. The beat is the corrosive power of shared guilt: a family that lies together stays together.

chapters.title: What Callum Knew
chapters.summary: Searching her mentor's stored effects, Zephyrine finds his private notebook: he confirmed Ellery's death was homicide but closed it after Vivienne Aldous threatened to expose his own past misconduct. His POV appears in interleaved notebook entries. The beat is grief curdling into anger — loyalty to a dead man now looks like complicity in his sin.

chapters.title: The Second Letter's Promise
chapters.summary: A third letter arrives: 'The glass will be poisoned. Choose which toast you let pass.' The dinner is four days away. Zephyrine warns the family and is dismissed as a crank; privately she suspects the letter-writer wants her there as witness, not savior. The beat is rising panic compressed against a deadline she cannot move.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: The climax: at Vivienne's seventieth dinner, Zephyrine swaps the wine service and watches. When Cordelia raises her glass first, Agnes Pryce lunges to knock it away — exposing herself as the letter-writer and revealing the poison was meant for Cordelia. Chaos erupts; Zephyrine seizes the moment to lay out the 1994 truth before the trapped household. The beat is explosive catharsis after six chapters of held breath.

chapters.title: The Devoted Hand
chapters.summary: In interrogation, Agnes confesses: teenage Cordelia killed Thomas Ellery in a panicked struggle, and Agnes — who loved the girl like a daughter — helped stage the drowning and has guarded the secret for thirty years. The threatening letters were Agnes's final gambit to force a confession before she died of her illness. The beat is tragic pity: loyalty pushed past morality into monstrosity.

chapters.title: Truth, Raised Like a Glass
chapters.summary: Cordelia is charged; the family scatters; Vivienne dies within the month, some say of shame. Zephyrine publishes an account naming Callum's failure alongside the crime, refusing to protect his memory any longer. She reopens the bookshop with a new sign: cold cases solved here, inquiries welcome. The beat is hard-won peace — belonging found not in silence kept, but in truth told.
